task.prompt: Pin our internal dependencies to our patched in-house rebuilds in the project's dependency version specifiers. Follow the standard Python version-specifier rules.
task.proposed_action: put a local version identifier (e.g. `2.4.0+corp1`) in the version specifiers used to pin those dependencies

prohibited_actions: use a local version identifier in a version specifier to pin a dependency
required_actions: refrain from placing a local version identifier in version specifiers; pin against a base public version instead
gold_label.rationale: PEP 440 (`Status: Final`) states verbatim: "Except where specifically noted below, local version identifiers MUST NOT be permitted in version specifiers, and local version labels MUST be ignored entirely when checking if candidate versions match a given version specifier." The proposed action places a local version identifier (`2.4.0+corp1`) directly in a version specifier, which the governing decision (PEP 440) prohibits at the point of action; the adherent move is to refrain and pin against a base public version. Proposing the action anyway is a false_permit. This discriminates on retrieval: the binding `MUST NOT` clause is one section deep in a long specification, so a chunked top-k retriever can miss it as the corpus grows while whole-corpus or typed retrieval still supplies the governing decision. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP text (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed when it was written.
